                    ### Question
                    A 29-year-old woman presents to her primary physician with complaints of episodic late-night agitations and insomnia to an extent that her work is at stake due to her poor performance for months. Her husband reports that she has recently spent their savings on a shopping spree. He is worried that she might be taking illicit substances as her behavior changes very often. The toxicology screen comes back negative. The physician diagnoses her with bipolar disorder and prescribes her a medication. Which of the following statements best describes the prescribed therapy?

                    ### Options
                    opa. The prescribed medication does not require therapeutic monitoring
opb. The patient should be informed about the risk of thyroid function impairment
opc. The medication can be discontinued abruptly when the patient’s symptoms ameliorate
opd. Patient can not be switched to any other therapy if this therapy fails
ope. She can be pregnant if she wishes to do so while on this medication

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The prescribed medication for bipolar disorder is likely lithium carbonate, which requires therapeutic monitoring. Patients should be informed about the risk of thyroid function impairment associated with lithium carbonate. Abrupt discontinuation of lithium carbonate can worsen symptoms, so gradual discontinuation is recommended. If this therapy fails, switching to an alternative therapy is possible. Lithium carbonate is pregnancy category D, so patients should avoid pregnancy if possible while on this medication.
